notes: 4 beam pieces under a slab analysed as a shell: on the slab's nodes, their own axis below by rigid arms (the slab and the beam work as a T).

Shells (S2): 96 elements (96 MITC4 quadrilaterals, 0 MITC3 triangles) on 1 surface, mesh 0.5 m (at least 4 elements across a narrow piece); the slabs' loads stay on them, the 45° rule only where a slab is not a shell.
4 supports on springs (PF 180×180): 4 nodes, 4 on Winkler's bed (kz = ks·A, the footprint's ks·I against turning; across and along a strip each node its length); the springs' forces are reactions.
4 support nodes in compression only: each combination solved again where one would pull, lifted (free).
Bars as Timoshenko beams, their shear areas from the section (EN 1993-1-1 §6.2.6(3) for steel, 5/6·A for a rectangle).

Second order (P-Δ): each static combination solved with the bars' geometric stiffness of their axial forces, iterated; the cases stay first order. Along a bar the moment keeps its first-order shape between its ends: its own buckling is its check's (EN 1993-1-1 6.3).
The shells have no geometric stiffness: second order and buckling are the bars' only.
Second order amplifies the sway most in „1.35 G1 + 1.5 Q-A + 0.75 S + 0.9 W-Y/s + φ(−X)”: × 212.144.

Global sway imperfections (EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2; the same form for concrete, EN 1992-1-1 5.2; timber by EN 1995-1-1 5.4.4): each ultimate combination solved four times, ±X and ±Y, with φ·NEd at the top and −φ·NEd at the foot of each compressed column, NEd of its first-order result; h = 2.9 m, αh = 1, φ up to 1/200 along X (m = 1), φ up to 1/200 along Y (m = 1). A combination's results are the envelope of its four.
